about: Target ranges for the coding-comparison scorecard, transcribed from docs/LITERATURE_PLACE_FIELDS_POPULATION_SIMILARITY.md (the review). Each entry keeps the review's verification tag. Values marked 'derived (this suite)' are arithmetic done here on numbers the review reports, with the formula given. Nothing is rounded toward the models. A region with no number for a measure has no entry and scores 'untestable'.

schema.row: scorecard row this target is scored on (see scorecard.py ROWS)
schema.environment: the recording's environment, as the review gives it
schema.kind: range | point | upper | lower | bool | curve | info (info entries are listed but not scored)
schema.tol: rel: a point is consistent within +-30% of its value; abs: within +-0.1 (used for correlations and similarities); none: the band is exactly low..high
schema.tag: the review's verification tag, plus 'derived (this suite)' where this file does the arithmetic
schema.primary: true if this entry decides the scorecard cell; other entries for the same cell are listed beside it

policy.why: A literature point without a reported spread needs some band before a model value can be called consistent with it. These two widths are the suite's choice, stated once and applied to every point target; range targets use the reported range exactly.

rich2014.zero_fraction_formula: P(0 | L_W) = (7.75 / (7.75 + 0.65 * L_W)) ** 0.57, with L_W the track length in mean field widths
